title: A message from Emma
situation_ru: Подруга оставляет длинное голосовое сообщение о первой неделе на новой работе.
script: Emma: Hi Sarah, it's Emma. Sorry I missed your call, I was still at work. I just wanted to tell you how my first week at the new job went. [pause 1s] Well, it's been tiring, to be honest. The office is much bigger than my old one, and I got lost twice on Monday! But everyone has been really friendly. My manager, Paul, took me out for lunch on my first day, and the woman who sits next to me has already shown me all the best places to get coffee. Oh, and the canteen is amazing: the food is cheap and really healthy. [pause 1s] The work itself is more interesting than I expected. In my old job I did the same thing every day, but here every project is different. The only thing I'm not happy about is the journey. It takes almost an hour each way, and the trains are always packed. I'm thinking about cycling instead when the weather gets better. [pause 1s] Anyway, are you free on Friday evening? I'd love to celebrate surviving my first week! Text me, OK? Bye.

title: Getting a dog?
situation_ru: Двое соседей по квартире обсуждают, не завести ли собаку.
script:
Jake: So, I've been thinking. What do you think about getting a dog?
Nina: A dog? In this apartment? Jake, we can barely fit the two of us in here.
Jake: I know it's small, but there's a big park just across the street. I'd walk him every morning before work.
Nina: Every morning? You can't even get up in time for breakfast!
Jake: OK, that's fair. But I really think it would be good for us. We both work from home a lot, so he wouldn't be alone all day.
Nina: That's true. But what about when we go away? Last summer we were away for three weeks.
Jake: My parents could look after him. They've always had dogs.
Nina: Hmm. I'm not saying no. I just don't want us to rush into it. Dogs live for fifteen years or more.
Jake: So how about this? My cousin needs someone to look after her dog for a week in May. We could try it and see how it goes.
Nina: Now that's a good idea. Let's do that first.

questions.q: How does Nina react to Jake's idea at first?
options: She's excited and wants a dog soon
She's angry that Jake didn't ask her opinion earlier
She's doubtful because the apartment is small
She says she doesn't like dogs at all
questions.explain_ru: Нина сомневается: в квартире им и двоим тесно.

questions.q: Why does Jake think the dog wouldn't be lonely?
options: They often work from home
His parents live very close by
There's a park across the street
Nina doesn't go out very much
questions.explain_ru: Они оба часто работают из дома.

questions.q: Why does Nina doubt that Jake will walk the dog every morning?
options: He doesn't like walking
He usually gets up late
The park opens late
She wants to walk it herself
questions.explain_ru: Джек даже на завтрак не успевает встать — значит, встаёт поздно.

questions.q: What do they decide to do?
options: Buy a puppy together in May
Move to a bigger apartment with a garden for a dog
Forget the idea completely
Look after his cousin's dog for a week first
questions.explain_ru: Сначала попробуют неделю присмотреть за собакой кузины.

situation_en: Two flatmates are talking about getting a dog.

title: Working late
situation_ru: Коллега замечает, что сотрудница перерабатывает, и даёт совет.
script:
Tom: You look exhausted, Rachel. Are you OK?
Rachel: Not really. I've been working until ten every night this week, and I still haven't finished the report.
Tom: Ten? That's crazy. When's the deadline?
Rachel: Friday. And the client keeps changing what they want.
Tom: Have you told Mark? He's your manager, he should know.
Rachel: I don't want him to think I can't cope.
Tom: Honestly, I think he'd rather know now than find out on Friday. Last year I did exactly what you're doing, and I ended up getting ill for two weeks. It wasn't worth it.
Rachel: I didn't know that.
Tom: Yeah, it was a horrible time. I was so stressed that I couldn't sleep properly. Now I try to stop at six, even when I'm busy, and I go for a run instead of checking emails. It really helps.
Rachel: I'm not sure I can stop at six this week. But maybe I'll talk to Mark tomorrow morning.
Tom: Good. And if you need help with the charts, just ask. I've got some free time on Thursday.
Rachel: Thanks, Tom. That would really help.

options: She's been working very late on a report
She's had an argument with her manager Mark
She's just been ill for two weeks
She's been going running every evening
questions.explain_ru: Всю неделю она работает до десяти вечера над отчётом.

To show what can happen if you overwork

Go for a run after work

title: Small Changes
situation_ru: Ведущий подкаста рассказывает, как начал ездить на работу на велосипеде.
script: Host: Hi, and welcome back to Small Changes, the podcast about little things that can make a big difference. Today I want to talk about something I started two years ago: cycling to work. [pause 1s] I'll be honest, the first month was terrible. I live about five miles from my office, and on my first day I arrived red, sweaty and twenty minutes late. My colleagues thought it was hilarious. But I didn't give up. I bought a better bike, found a quieter route along the river, and started keeping a clean shirt at the office. [pause 1s] Now, two years later, I can't imagine going back to the car. I save around a hundred dollars a month on gas and parking, I've lost a few pounds, and, most importantly, I arrive at work in a much better mood. There's something about starting the day outside that clears your head. [pause 1s] Of course, it's not perfect. When it's raining hard, I still take the bus. And it isn't for everyone. If you live thirty miles away, it's probably not realistic. But if your office is close, why not try it just once a week?

He fell off his bike near the river
questions.explain_ru: Он приехал красный, вспотевший и на 20 минут позже.

questions.explain_ru: Most importantly — он приезжает на работу в хорошем настроении.
